The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring caller to be both admin and owner so team admins get FORBIDDEN
EventManager constructed with requesting user's credentials instead of booking organizer, breaking calendar attendee updates for non-organizer adders

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` where `eventManager` is constructed from the requesting session user (`const { user } = ctx; ... new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`) and credentials are loaded with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The handler explicitly allows non-organizers (team admin/owner or an attendee) to add guests, but in those cases it will still use the non-organizer’s credentials rather than the booking organizer’s credentials (which are available on `booking.user.credentials` via the `include`). This is a concrete mismatch in the diff and can plausibly break updating the organizer’s calendar event when the requester isn’t the organizer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email comparison is case-sensitive in uniqueGuests filter allowing duplicate attendee rows via createMany

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out existing attendees using `guest === attendee.email` and blacklisted guests using `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., to lowercase). Since JavaScript string equality and `includes` are case-sensitive, providing `Test@Example.com` when `test@example.com` already exists will bypass the duplicate check and proceed to `createMany`, potentially creating a duplicate attendee row (or triggering a DB error if a unique constraint exists). The same issue applies to the blacklist check because the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist compares lowercased env values against raw guest string, letting case-varied emails bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
In sendAddGuestsEmails, newGuests.includes(attendee.email) case-sensitivity sends wrong email type for case-differing guests

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the branch `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` is a strict, case-sensitive comparison. The `addGuestsHandler` passes `guests` (the raw input array) as `newGuests` without normalizing case, and attendee emails (`calendarEvent.attendees[].email`) come from the DB. Since email local-parts are typically treated case-insensitively in practice, a guest added as `Test@Example.com` could be stored/compared as `test@example.com`, making `includes` return false and causing the code to send the wrong template (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` instead of the intended `AttendeeScheduledEmail` for the newly added guest). This is a concrete correctness bug present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Errors in email sending swallowed by catch that only console.logs a message without the error object, returning success

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the code wraps `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` and ignores the caught `err` entirely. After the catch, the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` unconditionally, so email-sending failures are silently swallowed and the mutation reports success even when emails were not sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema does not validate guest uniqueness among themselves, allowing duplicate attendee rows from API callers
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the input guest list is not deduplicated/validated for uniqueness within itself, so repeated emails from the client can lead to duplicate attendee rows being inserted (e.g., via createMany).

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails passed raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, so filtered-out emails get wrong email classification
Validation error state in AddGuestsDialog never clears when user corrects emails

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. Editing/correcting emails via `MultiEmail` only calls `setMultiEmailValue` and never clears `isInvalidEmail`, and the success path also doesn’t reset it before closing. So the validation error message persists even after the user corrects the inputs (until Cancel/close).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog silently no-ops when email list is empty, giving no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.handleAdd(), the first check is `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` with no toast/message/state update. `multiEmailValue` can become `[]` because MultiEmail’s remove handler does `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`; removing the last remaining email field leaves an empty array. In that state, the dialog still renders the footer and the "Add" button, so clicking "Add" will silently do nothing (no mutation, no validation error UI, no toast).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || so a user must be both team admin and owner, making the check effectively organizer-or-attendee only

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. With `&&`, a user must be *both* a team admin and a team owner to satisfy this flag. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore deny access to team admins who aren’t owners (and owners who aren’t admins), contrary to the variable name and the likely intended “admin OR owner” semantics. This is a concrete, verifiable authorization logic bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Passing teamId ?? 0 to isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner for non-team bookings is meaningless and unsafe if changed to || without guarding null teamId

adjudication.rationale: In the added addGuests handler, the code uses `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` when calling `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner`. This does not introduce a verifiable bug by itself: for non-team bookings `teamId` becomes `0`, which will typically just make both checks return false and fall back to the organizer/attendee permission checks. The finding’s main claim (“unsafe if changed to `||` without guarding null teamId”) is hypothetical and not a problem present in the diff. Any actual correctness issue here is different (the code uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which likely should be `||`), but that is not what the proposed finding asserts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed with the caller's (attendee's) credentials instead of the organizer's (booking.user's) credentials, so calendar updates may fail silently or target the wrong calendars

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly allows a non-organizer attendee to call it (`isAttendee` passes the permission check). However, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` and `credentials` come from `ctx.user` (the caller) via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The organizer is fetched separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but their credentials are never used to construct the `EventManager`. This means when an attendee (or other permitted non-organizer) adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the caller's credentials rather than the booking owner's, which can cause calendar updates to fail or act on the wrong connected calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-attendee email uniqueness checks are case-sensitive (strict ===), allowing duplicate attendees like Bob@Example.com vs bob@example.com

adjudication.rationale: Yes. Both the client-side uniqueness refine and the server-side de-duplication logic are case-sensitive. In `AddGuestsDialog`, uniqueness is checked via `new Set(emails)` without normalizing case, so `Bob@Example.com` and `bob@example.com` are considered different. On the server in `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing-attendee filtering uses `guest === attendee.email` (also case-sensitive), so a guest email differing only by case from an existing attendee will be treated as “unique” and inserted via `createMany`. This matches the proposed finding and is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: sendAddGuestsEmails uses the raw input guests list (newGuests) when deciding who is a 'new guest' while iterating over the event's full attendees list, leading to incorrect classification and potentially sending the wrong/redundant email type. adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send errors are swallowed with no logging detail (err is discarded in catch block)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch`, but the `catch (err)` block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log/propagate `err`. This swallows the error details and makes failures harder to diagnose, matching the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side cap on the number of guests added per call, enabling mass-email/spam vector

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` (or other limit) in `addGuests.schema.ts`, and `addGuests.handler.ts` will (1) `createMany` those attendees and (2) call `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates attendees and sends emails. With no server-side cap, an authorized caller (including an existing attendee per `isAttendee`) can submit a very large array and trigger large DB writes and bulk outbound emails, creating an abuse/spam vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array in addGuests.schema.ts: z.array(z.string().email()) has no .max(), allowing arbitrary number of attendees leading to unbounded createMany, calendar API updates, and email fan-out (resource exhaustion)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `{ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` with no upper bound. In `addGuestsHandler`, the `guests` array (after filtering) is used in `attendees.createMany` and then drives additional work: building attendee translations, calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out emails across attendees and team members. With no `.max()` (or other server-side limit), a permitted caller can submit a very large `guests` array and trigger large DB writes and email/calendar fan-out, creating a clear resource-exhaustion/spam vector present in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 translation queries per attendee in addGuests.handler.ts:113-121: getTranslation is called once per attendee, re-translating all existing attendees plus new ones on every guest addition instead of caching per distinct locale

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, after updating the booking, it iterates over bookingAttendees.attendees (which includes all existing attendees plus the newly added ones) and for each attendee does `translate: await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")` (lines ~113-121). This results in one getTranslation call per attendee on every add-guests operation, even when many attendees share the same locale and even though the organizer translation is already fetched separately. There is no per-locale caching/deduplication, so the N-per-attendee repeated translation loads are real and directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email fan-out in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:522-545) sends emails to organizer, all team members, and every attendee of the booking on each add operation rather than just the new guests, resulting in O(N×M) emails and leaking full booking details to new guests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `sendAddGuestsEmails` which unconditionally enqueues emails to (1) the organizer (`emailsToSend.push(new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail(...))`), (2) every team member if `calendarEvent.team?.members` exists (loop pushing another `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` per member), and (3) *every attendee* in `calendarEvent.attendees` via `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`, choosing between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` based on whether the attendee is in `newGuests`. In the handler, `evt.attendees` is built from `bookingAttendees.attendees` after the DB update, i.e., it includes both existing and newly added guests, so each “add guests” operation will email all attendees, not just the newly added ones. The “leaking full booking details to new guests” part is not directly verifiable from this diff (new guests are intended recipients), but the fan-out/spam-to-all-attendees behavior is clearly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant generateIcsString per recipient in attendee-add-guests-email.ts and organizer-add-guests-email.ts: each email independently builds an identical ICS string

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `generateIcsString(...)` being called inside `getNodeMailerPayload()` for both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, so it will be executed once per email sent. However, this is a performance/micro-optimization observation, not a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the change. Also, the ICS is not strictly “identical” across both templates because the `role` differs (`attendee` vs `organizer`), even if it is likely identical across recipients within the same template. A reasonable reviewer would treat this as optional optimization rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: replyTo header in organizer-add-guests-email.ts:34 builds an unbounded reply-to list that grows with attendee count, potentially producing oversized SMTP headers rejected by mail servers

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, `replyTo` is constructed as `[this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`, which scales linearly with attendee count and has no cap or truncation. That is verifiably “unbounded” in the sense that any booking with many attendees will generate a very long Reply-To header, increasing the risk of exceeding email header size limits and being rejected by MTAs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant permission queries in addGuests.handler.ts:48-50: isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner are both awaited unconditionally and sequentially even when caller is organizer or attendee; also the && logic requires being both admin AND owner which is likely a logic bug

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the permission flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This both (1) awaits two permission queries unconditionally before checking `isOrganizer`/`isAttendee`, so even organizers/attendees pay the cost of both DB checks, and (2) uses `&&`, meaning the user must be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner to satisfy `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. Given the variable name and later check `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this will incorrectly deny access to team admins who are not owners (a plausible correctness/authorization bug). Both issues are directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Over-fetched booking record in addGuests.handler.ts:26-42: initial findFirst includes user.credentials (large JSON blobs) though only organizer basic fields are used and credentials are fetched separately later

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the initial prisma.booking.findFirst includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`. Later in the handler, only `booking.user?.destinationCalendar` is used; `booking.user.credentials` is never referenced. Credentials are fetched separately via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, so including `user.credentials` in the booking query is unnecessary extra data fetching (potentially large blobs) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive dedupe in addGuests.handler.ts:62-66: booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) compares emails case-sensitively while other comparisons use .toLowerCase(), allowing Foo@x.com vs foo@x.com to bypass dedupe and create duplicate rows

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: in `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing case, while `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased. This allows `Foo@x.com` vs `foo@x.com` to bypass both the “already an attendee” check and blacklist check, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows differing only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic bug: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, denying users who are only admin or only owner
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same authorization logic issue: using AND (&&) for admin/owner permission checks incorrectly requires both roles, and it should be OR (||) to allow either role.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When eventType is null, teamId evaluates to ?? 0 so both role queries run against team 0 unnecessarily

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code does pass `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` into `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, so when `eventType`/`teamId` is missing it will call at least `isTeamAdmin` with teamId `0`. However, the finding claims “both role queries run” in that case, which is not verifiably true because the expression uses `&&` with `await` and will short-circuit: `isTeamOwner(...)` is only invoked if `isTeamAdmin(...)` resolves truthy. So the specific behavior described (“both queries run”) is not reliably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side Zod schema ZAddGuestsInputSchema does not enforce guest email uniqueness, so duplicate emails in the guests array create duplicate attendee records via createMany

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts only validates `guests` as an array of emails (`z.array(z.string().email())`) and does not enforce uniqueness. In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the provided `guests` array. Therefore an input like `["a@example.com","a@example.com"]` (when not already an attendee) will produce duplicate entries in `guestsFullDetails` and be passed to `attendees.createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows (or causing a DB error if constrained). Frontend uniqueness validation exists but is not sufficient as server protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive guest dedupe against existing attendees (exact ===) while blacklist comparison lowercases emails, allowing John@Example.com to bypass dedupe of john@example.com and break email template selection

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, existing-attendee dedupe is case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, so `John@Example.com` will not match an existing `john@example.com` and will be treated as a “unique” guest, creating a duplicate attendee differing only by case. Additionally, blacklist entries are lowercased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the input `guest` is not normalized before `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, so a blacklisted email can bypass the blacklist via casing. Finally, sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw `guests` array (not `uniqueGuests` nor normalized), and uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (also case-sensitive) to choose which template to send, so casing mismatches can lead to incorrect template selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests, causing newGuests.includes check to misfire and send wrong email variant to existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, and only `uniqueGuests` are actually persisted via `createMany`. However, when sending emails it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests`, not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the email variant is chosen via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ...`, so if the caller included an existing attendee’s email in the input (or other filtered-out emails), that attendee will be treated as “new” even though they weren’t added, causing the wrong email template to be sent. Passing `uniqueGuests` would align email logic with the actual added guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic operation: DB attendees persisted before calendar update, so calendar failure leaves inconsistent state with no rollback or partial-failure indication

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees to the DB first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` (assigned to `bookingAttendees`), and only afterwards calls the external side-effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no surrounding transaction/rollback or compensating action. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (network/provider failure, credential issues, etc.), the handler will error out after the DB write, leaving the booking attendees updated in the database but not reflected in the calendar system. This is a real non-atomic/partial-failure inconsistency introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send errors swallowed by bare try/catch that only console.logs a message without logging the err

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the new code wraps `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` in a `try/catch` and, on error, only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err` or rethrowing/handling it. This swallows the actual exception details, making failures hard to diagnose and potentially masking operational issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side validation error state (isInvalidEmail) never resets while user edits email fields, only cleared on Cancel

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is never cleared on input change (`MultiEmail` only calls `setMultiEmailValue`) and `handleAdd` does not set it back to `false` on successful validation/mutation. The only explicit reset is in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Therefore, after one invalid attempt, the validation error will persist while the user edits fields until they cancel/close the dialog.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking lookup by bare bookingId has no ownership scoping; isAttendee grants any attendee of any booking guest-add rights, broader than intended permission surface

adjudication.rationale: In addGuestsHandler, the booking is fetched by id, but authorization is enforced immediately after: it allows the action only if the user is (a) organizer (booking.userId === user.id), (b) an attendee of that same booking (booking.attendees contains user.email), or (c) team admin/owner. The proposed finding’s claim that “isAttendee grants any attendee of any booking guest-add rights” is not supported by the diff: isAttendee is computed from the fetched booking’s attendees, so it is inherently scoped to that bookingId. While fetching by bare id could enable existence probing (NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN), that’s a different issue than the one stated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses && instead of || for isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring user to be both admin and owner so plain admins are denied access

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. That contradicts the variable name and common intent (“admin or owner”). As written, a user who is an admin but not an owner will fail this check and be denied unless they are also the organizer or an attendee (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, causing updateCalendarAttendees to fail or no-op when a non-organizer adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update path builds an `EventManager` with `...user` and credentials from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the requesting user), then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. However, the booking organizer is separately fetched as `organizer`, and the booking’s calendar integrations/credentials are associated with `booking.user` (included in the booking query), not necessarily the requester. Since the handler explicitly allows non-organizers (attendees, and team admins/owners) to add guests, this code will attempt to update the organizer’s event using the non-organizer’s credentials, which is likely to fail/no-op when the requester doesn’t have access to the organizer’s connected calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If the organizer lacks credentials, an unhandled error may throw after the DB write has committed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB write happens first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and commits before any external side effects. After that, the code calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and then `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` **without** a surrounding `try/catch` (unlike `sendAddGuestsEmails`, which is caught). If the acting user (often the organizer, but could also be an attendee/admin) has no/invalid calendar credentials or `updateCalendarAttendees` throws for any reason, the mutation will error out after the DB update has already been persisted, leaving a partial update (DB attendees added, but calendar + emails not updated) and an unhandled exception path in this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB write is not transactional with calendar side effects; calendar failure after DB commit leaves inconsistent state and user retry hits emails_must_be_unique errors

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})`, and only afterward it performs calendar side effects with `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. There is no transaction/compensation around these steps. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation aborts after the DB commit, leaving guests persisted in the DB but not reflected in external calendars. A subsequent retry with the same emails will compute `uniqueGuests` as empty (because they now exist in `booking.attendees`) and throw `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, preventing a simple retry to re-run the calendar update. This matches the proposed finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure is swallowed with no error details — catch block discards err and only logs a generic message

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email-sending call is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The catch block neither rethrows nor logs `err`, so failures are silently swallowed and diagnostic details are lost, matching the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email dedup comparison is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendees, calendar invites, and emails for case-variant emails

adjudication.rationale: Yes. Both client and server-side “deduplication”/existing-attendee checks are case-sensitive. In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, uniqueness is enforced via `new Set(emails)` without normalizing case, so `Test@x.com` and `test@x.com` pass as “unique”. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing attendees are filtered with `guest === attendee.email` (case-sensitive), and blacklist checking uses `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` while the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not, so case-variant emails can bypass the blacklist and be inserted as additional attendees, leading to duplicate invites/emails for the same mailbox in many systems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail is never reset after shown, so the stale error banner persists after the user corrects emails or resubmits successfully

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails in `handleAdd`, but it’s only reset in the Cancel button handler. It is not reset when the user edits `MultiEmail` (no `onChange` hook clears it) and not reset on successful submission (`onSuccess` closes dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Since the component remains mounted even when `Dialog` is closed, reopening after a successful add can still show the stale error banner.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails filters new guests against the unfiltered original guests list instead of uniqueGuests, sending wrong email type to existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuestsHandler`, the code computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only creates new attendee records from `uniqueGuests`. However it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original, unfiltered `guests` array. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the email type selection is driven by `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` while iterating over *all* `calendarEvent.attendees` (which includes existing attendees). If the user submitted an email that was already an attendee, that existing attendee will be present in `calendarEvent.attendees` and also present in the original `guests` list, causing them to be treated as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid that mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing server-side cap (max()) on the guests array in the schema, permitting resource exhaustion / email blasting from a single request

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. The handler `addGuestsHandler` uses this array to (1) `createMany` attendee records and (2) send emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates over attendees and triggers email sends. Since the server-side validation does not cap the array size, an authorized caller (even an attendee is permitted by `isAttendee`) could submit a very large `guests` list, causing excessive DB writes and outbound email sends in a single request (resource exhaustion / email blasting).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema defined inside component body on every render and duplicates/diverges from the shared server-side schema (server lacks the uniqueness refinement)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is created inside the component on every render (`const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(...).refine(...)`), so it is re-instantiated per render. More importantly, this client-side schema enforces uniqueness via `.refine(...)`, but the server-side `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. The handler also does not de-duplicate within the incoming `guests` array (it filters against existing attendees/blacklist only), so duplicate emails can still reach `createMany`, meaning client/server validation can diverge and duplicates can be inserted if called outside the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner logic uses && instead of ||, so a user who is admin-but-not-owner (or vice versa) fails the permission check

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass, which contradicts the variable name and typical authorization intent (“admin OR owner”). As written, a user who is admin-but-not-owner (or owner-but-not-admin) will fail `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` and be incorrectly forbidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking lookup in addGuests.handler.ts has no ownership scoping in the where clause; authorization is bolted on afterward with sentinel ?? 0 teamId

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the Prisma lookup does fetch the booking by id only (`where: { id: bookingId }`) and then performs authorization checks afterward. However, this pattern is not inherently a verifiable defect in the diff because the handler does gate all subsequent behavior with a permission check and does not return booking data before that. The `teamId ?? 0` is only used as an argument to `isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner` and does not weaken the query itself; it just results in a falsey team-admin check when there is no team. So while one could prefer scoping the query to reduce existence-disclosure, the finding claims a clear problem that isn’t conclusively demonstrated as a bug/security issue from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails passes unfiltered guests instead of uniqueGuests, so filtered-out duplicates can trigger wrong email templates for existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-attending emails and blacklisted ones) and only creates attendees for `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original unfiltered array. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the email template selection is based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`: attendees whose email is in `newGuests` get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, otherwise they get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the caller included an email that was already an attendee, that email will be present in `guests` but not in `uniqueGuests`, and the existing attendee will incorrectly match `includes(...)` and receive the wrong template (scheduled/invite) even though they weren't newly added. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Swallowed error in catch block using console.log, discarding the error object and reporting success regardless of email delivery failure

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and then the handler returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` without rethrowing or otherwise surfacing the failure. The caught `err` is also discarded (not logged/used). This means the mutation will succeed and the UI will show success (`onSuccess`) even if email delivery fails, and the actual error detail is lost.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side uniqueness validation in AddGuestsDialog is broken: multiEmailValue.length === 0 guard unreachable since MultiEmail starts as [""], and isInvalidEmail is never reset on successful retry
MultiEmail component mutates its own props (value = value || []) and uses index keys, causing stale input state when emails are removed mid-list

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `key={index}` in `MultiEmail` and it reassigns the local parameter `value = value || []`. However, that reassignment does not mutate the caller’s prop object/array; it only rebinds a local variable. The claimed “stale input state when emails are removed mid-list” due to index keys is not directly verifiable from the diff because the inputs are rendered as controlled (`value={field}`) and will re-render with the updated array after `splice`. Any true staleness would depend on `EmailField` having internal/uncontrolled state, which is not shown here. So the finding overstates a speculative issue rather than a clear defect introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded, untranslated "Remove email" tooltip bypassing the t() i18n function used elsewhere in the component

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the tooltip text is hardcoded as `Tooltip content="Remove email"` instead of using the existing i18n pattern (`const { t } = useLocale();` and `t("...")`) used elsewhere in the same component (e.g., `t("add_another")`). This introduces an untranslated UI string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: readOnly prop on MultiEmail is required but has no consumer in the PR — speculative dead API surface (YAGNI)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `MultiEmail` is actually used by the new `AddGuestsDialog`, which passes `readOnly={false}`. The `readOnly` prop is also actively consumed inside `MultiEmail` to disable the `EmailField` and to conditionally render/remove the remove/add controls. So this is neither unused nor “dead API surface” in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmailLazy.tsx contains a factually wrong 40kb comment and a double cast (as unknown as) copied from PhoneInputLazy, with confusing shadowed export naming

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` adds a dynamic import with a comment and a type assertion: `const MultiEmail = dynamic(() => import("./MultiEmail")) as unknown as typeof import("./MultiEmail").default;`. While the comment (“like 40kb”) may be unverifiable or potentially inaccurate, that’s not a code defect. The double cast is a common TypeScript workaround for `next/dynamic` typing and is not inherently incorrect or broken based on the diff. The naming (`const MultiEmail` exported as default) is not actually shadowing another identifier within the file and does not introduce a functional/correctness problem. Overall, the finding is primarily style/subjective rather than a real verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AttendeeAddGuestsEmail/organizer email templates duplicated across multiple paths (templates/ vs src/templates/), with copy-pasted ICS titles/subtitles using arguably wrong copy for 'guests added'

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds both `packages/emails/templates/*` (NodeMailer payload classes used by `email-manager.ts`) and `packages/emails/src/templates/*` (React template components used by `renderEmail`). This split already exists for other emails in the codebase (e.g., `AttendeeScheduledEmail` class vs `src/templates/AttendeeScheduledEmail` component), so having files in both locations is an expected pattern rather than an accidental duplication/defect. The claim about “arguably wrong copy” for ICS title/subtitle is subjective and not verifiably incorrect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated ~50-line CalendarEvent construction in addGuests.handler.ts replicating logic from editLocation, reschedule, and other handlers — should extract a getBookingCalendarEvent(booking) helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a ~50-line inline `CalendarEvent` object being constructed in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but the claim that it "replicates logic from editLocation, reschedule, and other handlers" is not verifiable from this diff because those other handlers’ implementations are not shown. Also, this is a refactor/maintainability suggestion (DRY) rather than a clear defect/bug introduced by the change. Therefore it’s not a concrete, verifiable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests")) fallback is unreachable, and raw error codes are interpolated into translated templates showing literal codes like BAD_REQUEST to users

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, onError builds `message` as a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literals always produce a non-empty string, even when `err.data?.code` is undefined (e.g. "undefined: …"), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"))` will never hit the fallback. Also, `err.data?.code` is a raw TRPC error code (e.g. "BAD_REQUEST", "FORBIDDEN") which will be shown directly to end users as part of the toast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BookingListItem adds the add_members menu item unconditionally with no gating on booking state (past/cancelled/confirmed)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an "add_members" menu item to the `menuItems` array without any condition inline, but the finding assumes this is a defect (“should be gated on past/cancelled/confirmed”) without showing (in the provided diff context) what booking-state gating exists elsewhere in `BookingListItem` (e.g., later filtering/disable logic when rendering the menu) or any requirement that this action must be hidden/disabled for certain states. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that this introduces a bug rather than an intentional always-available action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer query uses findFirstOrThrow with id: booking.userId || 0 sentinel value instead of proper null handling, producing opaque errors when userId is null

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. This explicitly substitutes `0` when `booking.userId` is falsy (e.g., `null/undefined`), which will cause `findFirstOrThrow` to throw a generic “record not found”/Prisma error rather than a deliberate, clear TRPC error for a missing organizer. The code already treats `booking.userId` as potentially absent elsewhere (`booking.userId || 0`, `booking.userId === user.id`), so this sentinel approach can produce opaque failures when `userId` is not set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring user to be both admin and owner to manage team bookings

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that check. Given the variable name and the later permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) FORBIDDEN`), a user who is *only* an admin (not owner) would be incorrectly denied. Unless `isTeamAdmin` is implemented to include owners (not shown in diff), this is a real logic/authorization bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization allows any booking attendee (including any guest email or user with matching email) to call the addGuests mutation

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation is an `authedProcedure` and the handler explicitly authorizes the caller if they are an attendee: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then allows the mutation when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` is false. That means any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee on the booking (including a previously-added guest attendee record) can call `addGuests` and add more guests, without needing to be the organizer/admin/owner.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check that the booking is not cancelled or in the past, allowing guests/ICS invites to be added to cancelled bookings

adjudication.rationale:
The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking and only checks permissions (team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee). It then updates `booking.attendees`, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sends ICS/email notifications via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`.

Nowhere in the added code path is there a check for booking state (e.g., cancelled) or timing (e.g., `startTime`/`endTime` in the past) before mutating attendees and emitting calendar/email updates. The UI also adds the “additional_guests” action unconditionally.

So the diff does introduce/contain the described gap: guests can be added and invites/emails sent even for cancelled/past bookings (assuming such states exist on `booking`, which is typical and not guarded against here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via case mismatch: blacklist emails are lowercased but guests compared without lowercasing
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes a blacklist bypass caused by lowercasing the blacklist but not lowercasing the guest emails before comparison, which is the same case-mismatch vulnerability described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate attendee check is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), allowing case-variant duplicates

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, uniqueGuests is computed with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, which compares emails with strict case-sensitive equality. Since the input `guests` values are not normalized (e.g., lowercased) and existing `attendee.email` values may differ in case, the code can treat case-variant addresses (e.g., `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com`) as distinct and create duplicate attendee records for the same mailbox.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-transactional partial failure: DB write succeeds but calendar update failure is not rolled back, causing a 500 after the DB write

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch and no Prisma transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., calendar provider/API failure), the mutation will error (500/TRPC error) after the DB write has already succeeded, leaving guests added in the DB but not reflected in the external calendar. There is no rollback mechanism in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending errors are swallowed with only a console.log while the mutation still returns success

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block that does not rethrow or return an error. The handler then proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" };`, so the mutation can return success even if email sending fails. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Emails sent using raw guests input instead of filtered uniqueGuests, emailing skipped/filtered guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB update uses `uniqueGuests` (filtered to exclude existing attendees and blacklisted emails), but the email notification call uses the raw `guests`: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` array is used to decide which email template each *existing* attendee receives (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ...`). If the caller provided an email that was filtered out (e.g., already an attendee), that attendee will still be in `calendarEvent.attendees` but will be incorrectly treated as a “new guest” because their email is present in the raw `guests` array. Passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid this misclassification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Newly added guests never receive an email or ICS invite; only organizer, team members, and existing attendees are emailed

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly sends emails to all `calendarEvent.attendees` in `sendAddGuestsEmails`. Newly added guests are included in `calendarEvent.attendees` because the handler updates the booking attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... include: { attendees: true })`) and then builds `attendeesList` from the updated attendees. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, for any attendee whose email is in `newGuests`, it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail(...)` (which is an email/ICS invite flow), and for others it sends `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail(...)`. So newly added guests do receive an email (and likely an ICS invite), even if the template choice may be debatable. The claim that they “never receive an email or ICS invite” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: booking.userId == null causes findFirstOrThrow to throw unhandled Prisma error resulting in a 500 instead of a TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined` (which the code itself anticipates by using `|| 0`), the query becomes `id: 0`, and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma “record not found” error. This error is not caught or converted into a `TRPCError`, so it will bubble up as an internal server error (500) rather than a controlled TRPC error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: showToast error path renders raw/undefined error string to users; fallback message is dead code since template string is always truthy

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always produces a (non-empty) string (e.g., `"undefined: ..."`), so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback will never be used, even when `err.data?.code` or `err.message` are missing/undefined. This can lead to user-facing toasts like `"undefined: undefined"` / raw-ish error content rather than the intended generic message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail mutates the value prop and uses [""] as empty state, so empty-state branch never renders and handleAdd treats [""] as content
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying problem: representing an empty MultiEmail state as [""] instead of [] leads to incorrect behavior (empty-state UI/logic not triggering and the empty string being treated as real content), which can cause validation/handling issues. The golden suggests starting with [] and handling emptiness in the component; the candidate describes the consequences of using [""] and how it breaks logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No max() cap on guests array in schema, enabling mail-bomb/resource-exhaustion via thousands of emails in one mutation

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `addGuests` with `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defined as `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (and the client dialog similarly validates an unbounded array). There is no `.max(n)` (or other server-side limit) on the number of guest emails accepted. The handler then (a) `createMany` inserts all unique guests and (b) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which can trigger many outbound emails. This makes it verifiable that a single authorized caller could submit a very large `guests` array and force substantial DB/calendar/email work (resource exhaustion / mail-bomb potential).
